walkthroughs.body_html:
Miller's Tragedy and the Common Man (1949) defends the dignity of ordinary protagonists. Willy Loman's American Dream becomes his hamartia.

Modern tragedy democratises the form without abandoning its emotional structure.
Tennessee Williams's A Streetcar Named Desire (1947) sets Blanche DuBois's fall against post-war American class change. Domestic tragedy with mythic resonance.
Brecht rejected Aristotelian catharsis as politically anaesthetising. His epic theatre uses alienation devices (placards, songs, breaking the fourth wall) to keep audiences critical, not weeping.
